notes: Perfect agreement on ZF-CxxC domain-dependent, PRC1-independent targeting of KDM2B to CGIs. Both accept the genetic evidence from RING1B deletion and ZF-CxxC mutation experiments.
Strong agreement on KDM2B's specific recognition of non-methylated CpG DNA through EMSA and ChIP-seq. Reviewers implicitly accept these foundational findings without raising concerns.

LLM finds differential enrichment at polycomb sites fully supported. Reviewers accept the observation but question the mechanism (why KDM2A is excluded), indicating acceptance of data but uncertainty about interpretation.

LLM finds KDM2B-dependent RING1B targeting well-supported. Reviewers accept the widespread RING1B binding data but question why KDM2B presence alone is insufficient for robust PRC1 recruitment at most sites, indicating incomplete mechanistic understanding.

LLM finds complex composition rigorously established. Reviewers accept the interaction data but request clarification on mechanistic details (which PRC1 proteins, domains, why not CBX complexes), indicating data acceptance but mechanistic uncertainty.

Major disagreement on H2AK119ub1 findings. LLM accepts global reduction and locus-specific effects as supporting KDM2B's role. Reviewers find locus-specific loss 'not impressive' (~20%) and argue this challenges functional importance at derepressed genes.

LLM finds gene derepression data supported with appropriate validation. Reviewers question the logical inconsistency: if KDM2B is required for all RING1B binding, why does its loss only derepresses a small subset of genes?

LLM finds the H3K27me3-independent PRC1 targeting model well-supported by converging evidence. Reviewers accept core findings but find the overall model incomplete without explaining PRC2 recruitment and CBX-PRC1 targeting ('several links missing in the causal chain').

Agreement that widespread low-level RING1B at CGIs is observed but the 'sampling' interpretation is speculative. Both note lack of functional validation, though reviewers additionally question cell-type specificity.

Agreement that redundant targeting mechanisms and feed-forward loop models are reasonable but speculative interpretations lacking direct experimental validation. Both recognize these as frameworks requiring additional testing.

Partial overlap on spatial correlation claims (C38, C39). LLM finds overall enrichment pattern supported; reviewers accept correlation data but want mechanistic explanation for PRC2 co-localization at KDM2B/RING1B sites.
Agreement that KDM2B knockdown does not globally affect H3K27me3 or H3K4me3 (C61, C63). Both accept this finding as defining the specificity of KDM2B's role.
Agreement on knockdown validation showing specific KDM2B depletion without affecting other polycomb proteins (C50, C51). Both implicitly accept these technical controls.
Minimal overlap (C68 only). LLM finds overall model supported; reviewers question whether modest locus-specific H2AK119ub1 loss demonstrates functionally significant contribution to gene repression.
Agreement on knockdown specificity (C53). Both accept that KDM2B depletion is specific and does not affect other polycomb proteins.
Minimal overlap (C44 only on PCGF1). LLM finds complex composition well-established; reviewers want clarification on why KDM2B doesn't recruit CBX-containing complexes.
Minimal overlap (C67 on RING1B protein levels). LLM cites stable RING1B levels as ruling out indirect effects; reviewers accept this but have broader mechanistic questions about PRC1 interactions.

Minimal overlap (C54 on widespread RING1B). Both note the observation but question its interpretation - LLM finds 'sampling' model speculative; reviewers question why KDM2B alone is insufficient for robust recruitment.
Claim C24 about chromatin compaction only appears in peer review, where it is explicitly criticized as 'misguided assumption' given bivalent sites in ES cells. No corresponding LLM evaluation.
Claims C33-C34 about KDM2B nuclear localization only appear in peer review, where they are implicitly accepted. No corresponding LLM evaluation of this technical observation.
Claims C16-C17 about H3K36 demethylase activity at CGIs only appear in peer review, where reviewers question functional relevance. No corresponding LLM evaluation.
Claim C92 (part of LLM R1 on DNA binding specificity) has no corresponding peer review evaluation. LLM finds this aspect of DNA recognition supported.
Claim C36 (GO term enrichment for developmental genes) only appears in LLM results as part of supported enrichment analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation.
Claim C43 (reciprocal purifications validating interactions) only appears in LLM results as part of complex composition evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation.
Claim C65 (custom antibody validation) only appears in LLM results as part of H2AK119ub1 analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this technical control.
Claims C76-C77 (PRC1-PRC2 feed-forward loops) and C104 (redundancy models) only appear in LLM results, marked as speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation.
